cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has been teaching Israel that the LORD is God and there is no other, and that he won't be crossing the Jordan with them. Now he stops talking for a minute and gets to WORK. Friend, I once gave a whole speech on how to start a batch, and that batch NEVER got started.

cards.question: Moses sets aside some cities. True or false: these cities are on the west side of the Jordan, in the land Israel is about to cross into.
So the cities sit across the Jordan, to the east. How many cities does Moses set aside out there?

cards.text: These three cities are for a manslayer, a man who has killed his neighbor, but there's fine print. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer under instruction manuals nobody ever read, so trust me: READ THIS ONE.

cards.question: For a man who killed his neighbor to flee to one of these cities, how did it have to happen?

answers.text: By accident with no grudge beforehand
In a fight his neighbor started

cards.question: True or false: a man who planned it ahead of time, with malice in his heart, could also flee to one of these cities.
By fleeing to one of these cities, the manslayer could save his own ___.

cards.text: Quick map check, friend. Out east of the Jordan, the Reubenites and the Gadites got the land from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley, and the half-tribe of Manasseh got the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan.

Then Moses names all three cities, each with its own spot on the map, which is more labeling than I can manage. I once marked all six topping jars in my bakery TOPPINGS, and it took me a WEEK to find the sprinkles.

cards.question: The first city Moses names is Bezer, out east like the others. Where is Bezer?

answers.text: In the wilderness on the plateau
In the hill country of Ephraim

cards.question: Each city belongs to one of Israel's tribes. True or false: Bezer belongs to the Reubenites.
The other two cities each belong to a different tribe. Ramoth in Gilead belongs to the ___, and Golan in Bashan belongs to the ___.

findings.problem: The joke compares Moses moving from teaching to action with Papa Dorin giving a speech and never starting the batch. That is the opposite action, not the same one, so the comparison doesn't click. It can also read as a jab that Moses' teaching was all talk.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card tells only Deuteronomy 3:13-16, a tribal map from outside the passage. It doesn't tell any part of Deuteronomy 4:41-43 or move the baker forward through it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 8 says the half-tribe of Manasseh got all of Bashan, and that the Reubenites and Gadites got the land from Gilead down to the Arnon. That hands the baker card 12's answers: Golan in Bashan belongs to the Manassites, and once card 11 gives Bezer to Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead belongs to the Gadites.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question says Bezer is 'out east like the others', and cards 2 and 3 already placed the cities east of the Jordan. Both wrong answers, the hill country of Ephraim and the Negev of Judah, are well-known places west of the Jordan, so the setup rules them out. The right answer is the only one that fits the east.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 8 names only Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh as the tribes east of the Jordan. That rules out all three wrong answers (Benjamites, Danites, Ephraimites) before the baker reaches this card.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
